messages:
maria: Quick FYI — opened a small PR to switch inference-gateway svc from ClusterIP -> NodePort so we can attach an NLB with TLS passthrough. Need a quick secret binding + healthcheck sanity check before I merge. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/482

sunil: thanks — can you paste the Service + ingress/terraform snippets you changed? want to make sure we didn't accidentally change TLS termination. :eyes:

maria: sure, here's the k8s svc change i made (only the port bits):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-gateway
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-nlb-target-type: "ip"  # kept ip targets
spec:
  type: NodePort
  selector:
    app: inference-gateway
  ports:
    - name: tls
      port: 443
      targetPort: 8080
      nodePort: 32043
```
and in terraform i added an nlb listener with passthrough: 
```hcl
resource "aws_lb_listener" "nlb_tls" {
  load_balancer_arn = aws_lb.nlb.arn
  port              = 443
  protocol          = "TLS"
  default_action {
    type             = "forward"
    target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.gateway_tls.arn
  }
}
# target group uses protocol TCP and port 8080
```

maria: note i did NOT attach a certificate to the listener (TLS passthrough), so we expect backend to terminate TLS.

kevin: quick checklist:
- service annotation above is fine for NLB (ip target).
- verify healthcheck target type is ip and uses TCP or gRPC as appropriate.
- ensure backend pods are actually listening on 8080 with TLS if passthrough (not plaintext).
- confirm nodePort falls within our allowed range (32000-32767).

elaine: just flagging that our vault secret name changed last month from "gateway-tls" -> "inference-gateway-tls" for the certs. if anyone wired IAM role in terraform to fetch that secret, it might still expect old name.

maria: good catch. i didn't touch secrets in this PR — but since we're using passthrough, we actually shouldn't be fetching a cert into k8s at all. however, there are env vars in the deployment that reference the old secret name for mutual TLS with internal services, so that could be a problem.

sunil: can you grep the deployment for references? also check the k8s secret mount path in the daemonset for sidecars. if the deployment expects the cert and it's missing, pods will crashloop but healthchecks might still show healthy at node layer.

maria: doing a quick scan now — found one reference in deployment: `valueFrom: secretKeyRef: name: gateway-tls` (old). i'll update to inference-gateway-tls in this PR.

kevin: also double-check the NLB healthcheck config in terraform. we've seen issues where ALB healthcheck with TLS path vs TCP target mismatched. For NLB using IP targets, set `protocol = "TCP"` and `port = "traffic-port"` unless you want application-level checks.

deploy-bot: [deploy-checker] terraform plan succeeded for module "nlb" — no secrets changes detected. (:white_check_mark:)

maria: OK i pushed two small commits: updated secret ref in deployment + fixed target group protocol to TCP in terraform. PTAL @kevin @sunil — hoping for a quick review, then i'll merge and roll canary.

kevin: skimming now. if we keep passthrough, remember to update docs in infra/README about tls termination choices and add a note in the rollout checklist to verify pod TLS readiness. :memo:

sunil: one more nit — we should avoid hardcoding nodePort; prefer letting k8s choose unless we need a stable port for firewall rules. do we need a fixed port for security group?

maria: yes we need it for our node security group rule that only allows 32043 from the NLB subnets. if we let k8s pick we risk drift and extra SG churn. kept nodePort intentionally.

elaine: once merged, i'll run a quick smoke test against canary (staging) and verify mutual-tls handshakes and healthchecks. ping me when deployed. :+1:

maria: thanks all — will merge after reviews and tag you when canary is up.
